deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page, so there is no derivation to reconstruct. Folio 94 is a page of German lecture or reading notes on ancient Greek history: the last phase of the Peloponnesian War. It continues the previous page (Alcibiades, Cyrus the Younger, Lysander) and leads into the next page (terms of Athens' surrender, the Thirty Tyrants, Thrasybulus). The bundle name 'HB.Lagrange1816' is misleading for this leaf. The hand and content look like history notes, possibly by Gauss or someone in his circle; nothing on the page is a computation.

Content, in order:
(1) Lysander had given Sparta a navy, but it became hard to maintain after Callicratidas succeeded him.
(2) In 406 Callicratidas beat the Athenians under Conon off Lesbos. Conon lost much of his fleet and was shut up in the harbour of Mytilene.
(3) The Athenians made a last effort and built a new fleet. It defeated Callicratidas at the Arginusae islands, where he fell (406).
(4) The Athenians grew careless. Lysander returned to command and went to meet them at the Hellespont, where they lay at anchor.
(5) Alcibiades warned the Athenians. Lysander attacked while the crews were off their ships, and the battle was half won before they could board (Aegospotami).
(6) Athens could no longer build a fleet. After subjecting several allies, Lysander sailed to Athens and besieged it by land and sea (marginal date 405).

The marginal notes are '+ die Athener' (an insertion mark for line 6) and the dates 406, 406 and 405.
errors: Historical, not mathematical: the page dates Lysander's surprise attack at the Hellespont (Aegospotami) to 'noch 406'. The battle is conventionally dated to 405 BC; the marginal '405' sits with the start of the siege instead.

Simplification: Lysander did not formally return as navarch, since Spartan law forbade a second term. He held the title epistoleus with de facto command. Athens' capitulation came in 404 BC, which falls on the next page.
No mathematical errors are possible: the page contains no mathematics.

results.what: Narrative notes on the Ionian/Decelean War, 406–405 BC: Callicratidas, Conon at Mytilene, Arginusae, Aegospotami, siege of Athens
results.modern_name: Standard ancient-history narrative (Xenophon, Hellenica I–II; Diodorus XIII)
results.usually_credited_to: Xenophon, Diodorus Siculus (ancient sources); standard 18th/19th-century history textbooks

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only routine history notes on the end of the Peloponnesian War, with no mathematical content. Its only interest is biographical or archival: it shows non-mathematical material filed in a Gauss bundle.
transcription_corrections: Line 7: the marginal note '+ die Athener' on the image is an insertion for 'Nochmals rafften [die Athener] sich wieder auf'. The transcription renders this correctly as {+die Athener+}.
Lines 7–8: 'zu ver- / her[?]' is doubtful. The image reads roughly '...zu einer Flotte und zu ver- / fer.' The word is unclear and is probably a hyphenated word that has been misread.
'wie die ganze Besatzung[-...-] von den Schiffen waren': the image appears to read 'Besatzungen' with a struck syllable, i.e. 'wie die ganze Besatzung (crews) von den Schiffen [weg] waren'.
'Die lebten[?] hier[?] ganz in Freude[?]' is consistent with the image ('Die lebten hier ganz in Freude').
'noch mehr[?] sicher' may be 'nur noch mehr sicher'; the sense ('to lull them into even greater security') is unchanged.
Margin opposite line 6 reads '+ die Athener'. The date '406' opposite 'Lysander suchte...' and '405' opposite 'Athen zu Lande...' are correctly placed.
